meta.title: GenTech Cookbook — Filipino → Cincinnati Ingredient Substitution Engine
meta.purpose: For a Filipino dish, map every ingredient to what's buyable in Cincinnati, OH (Jordan's local Kroger + Jungle Jim's + CAM Asian Market). Approximate prices are more important than exact — the substitute IS the point.
meta.price_note: Prices are rough US averages (USD). Kroger street pricing varies. Exact price is secondary to knowing the substitute.

stores.kroger: Jordan's local Kroger — carries most everyday + many Asian staples
stores.jungle_jims: Jungle Jim's International Market (Fairfield / Union Township) — THE place for Filipino staples: Mama Sita's, Maggi, bagoong, cane vinegar
stores.cam: CAM International Market — Asian grocer, Filipino + Southeast Asian staples
stores.online: Amazon / Weee! / Asian Food Grocer for anything not local

ingredient_substitutions.substitute: Rice vinegar (unseasoned) OR white vinegar + pinch of sugar
ingredient_substitutions.note: Rice vinegar is the closest match — milder, slightly sweet like cane vinegar. Distilled white vinegar works in a pinch but is harsher; add a little sugar.

ingredient_substitutions.substitute: Tamarind paste OR packaged sinigang mix (Knorr/Mama Sita's)
ingredient_substitutions.where: Jungle Jim's or CAM (tamarind paste, sinigang mix) — Kroger may carry tamarind in international aisle
ingredient_substitutions.note: Sinigang mix is the cheat-code: a packet gives the exact sour-salty flavor. Tamarind paste is the more 'real' route.

ingredient_substitutions.substitute: Thai shrimp paste (kapi / gapi) OR Vietnamese mam tom
ingredient_substitutions.where: CAM or Jungle Jim's (Thai/Vietnamese aisle) — NOT at a standard Kroger
ingredient_substitutions.note: Thai shrimp paste is the closest. It's saltier/fermented differently but works. Barrio Fiesta is the Filipino brand to look for at Asian grocers.

ingredient_substitutions.substitute: Chayote IS available in the US — buy it fresh
ingredient_substitutions.note: No substitution needed — chayote is commonly stocked in US supermarkets, especially ones with a Hispanic section. If not found: zucchini or green papaya.

ingredient_substitutions.ingredient: chili leaves (sili leaves / dahon ng sili)
ingredient_substitutions.substitute: Baby spinach OR moringa leaves (malunggay) if available
ingredient_substitutions.where: Kroger (baby spinach always) — moringa at Asian grocers
ingredient_substitutions.note: Chili leaves are hard to find in the US. Spinach is the easy stand-in for the 'wilted greens' finish. Moringa (malunggay) is the truer substitute if an Asian grocer has it.

ingredient_substitutions.substitute: Thai/Vietnamese fish sauce (Red Boat, Three Crabs, Squid brand)
ingredient_substitutions.note: Easily found. Squid brand is the classic Filipino/Southeast Asian choice, at Asian grocers. Kroger carries Red Boat in the international aisle.

ingredient_substitutions.substitute: Kikkoman or any soy sauce (Silver Swan is the Filipino brand)
ingredient_substitutions.note: No issue. Silver Swan (Filipino) at Asian grocers is the authentic choice, but Kikkoman at Kroger works fine.

ingredient_substitutions.substitute: Liver pâté / liverwurst from the deli — OR skip (add a little more soy + tomato)
ingredient_substitutions.note: Chicken/tomato liver pâté is the closest. If unavailable, caldereta still works without it — the flavor is slightly less rich.

ingredient_substitutions.filipino_dish_use: Caldereta mix, sinigang mix, adobo mix
ingredient_substitutions.substitute: The actual branded mixes — buy at Jungle Jim's / CAM, or Amazon/Weee!
ingredient_substitutions.note: These are Filipino-specific brands. Jungle Jim's carries them. This is a case where the 'substitute' is just finding the authentic product.

ingredient_substitutions.substitute: Maggi Seasoning (liquid) OR MSG (Accent) OR chicken bouillon powder
ingredient_substitutions.where: Kroger (MSG/Accent, bouillon) — Maggi liquid in international aisle
ingredient_substitutions.note: Maggi Sarap granules are specific, but the umami goal is covered by liquid Maggi or plain MSG.

ingredient_substitutions.substitute: Canned coconut milk (Chaokoh, Aroy-D) — no substitution needed
ingredient_substitutions.note: Easily found in any US supermarket.

ingredient_substitutions.substitute: Ube halaya (cooked jam) from Asian grocer OR ube extract for flavor
ingredient_substitutions.note: Fresh ube is hard to find. Ube halaya jars or ube extract are the practical route.

ingredient_substitutions.filipino_dish_use: Spaghetti, Filipino-style hot dogs, fried dishes
ingredient_substitutions.substitute: The authentic UFC brand — at Asian grocers or online. Not easily subbed.
ingredient_substitutions.note: No good Western substitute — it's sweet and orange-red. Buy the real thing.

ingredient_substitutions.substitute: Bitter melon IS available at Asian grocers (fresh)
ingredient_substitutions.where: CAM, Jungle Jim's — sometimes Kroger's international produce
ingredient_substitutions.note: Available fresh at Asian markets. If truly stuck, the closest flavor is a small amount of zucchini + a bitter green, but it's not the same.

ingredient_substitutions.substitute: Okra IS available fresh in US
ingredient_substitutions.note: Easily found, especially in the South/Midwest summer.
